definitions.gloss: excuse; evasion; pretext; talking one's way out
definitions.explanation: An attempt to avoid responsibility or blame through words, excuses, or explanations that deflect the issue. Carries a negative connotation — the excuse is seen as dishonest or inadequate.

examples.japanese: それはただの{言|い}い{逃|のが}れだ。
{言|い}い{逃|のが}れはやめて、{正直|しょうじき}に{話|はな}してください。
examples.english: Stop making excuses and speak honestly.

examples.japanese: {証拠|しょうこ}を{突|つ}きつけられて、もう{言|い}い{逃|のが}れができなくなった。
examples.english: Confronted with evidence, he could no longer talk his way out of it.

notes:
USAGE:
Always negative in connotation. The speaker views the excuse as dishonest, insufficient, or evasive. Can also be used as a verb: {言|い}い{逃|のが}れる (to talk one's way out of something).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {言|い}い{逃|のが}れをする (to make excuses)
- {言|い}い{逃|のが}れができない (to be unable to make excuses)
- ただの{言|い}い{逃|のが}れ (just an excuse)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {言|い}い{訳|わけ}: excuse — broader term, can be neutral or negative
- {弁解|べんかい}: justification, defense — more formal, implies defending one's actions
- {逃|に}げ{口上|こうじょう}: evasive excuse — a prepared excuse to escape responsibility
